title: Y Cynfod
summary: A gathering of faceless clay figures, given shifting presence by projected light and sound. Y Cynfod follows the impulse to make, from clay and fire to paint and code, and asks what it means for matter to become aware of itself.

cover.alt: We Were Here: clay figures with projected light

meta: Shades of Existence · 26 June–5 July 2026 · Curated by Hannah Jones

items: Y Cynfod, the before-beings, are faceless clay figures poised at the threshold of becoming a person. Their uneven bodies retain the marks of making; their lack of features leaves identity open. They give a human shape to a question that runs through the project: how does matter come to recognise itself?

Developed for Shades of Existence at Elysium Gallery, the work brings clay, projection, moving image, sound, painting and storytelling into a shared world. In We Were Here, projected colour finds the figures and moves on, changing their visibility without removing their presence. The CRT video smallfires imagines their origin through fire, light and sound. Paintings and a short story carry that world beyond the installation.

At its centre is a continuity between old and new ways of making. Shaping clay, tending fire, painting a figure and writing code all begin with the desire to give form to something felt. The project approaches existence through warmth, attention and the traces people leave: an invitation to spend time with these small presences, and to recognise something of our own unfinishedness in them.

title: The Shape of Things to Come
subtitle: Autumn 2026
summary: Lighting, sound and video design for a season of new performances, each shaped through collaboration with a different artist.

cover.alt: View from the street through a large window, with audiences inside and outside watching a winged performer in a pale set under cool light.
cover.caption: If You Had Wings · Angharad Matthews. Photo: Jamie Panton.

items: Across the autumn season at Volcano, I designed lighting, sound and video for a changing programme of new performance. Each collaboration called for a different relationship between the performer, the room, the image and the sound.
My work brought the three design disciplines together, responding to each artist’s language and the practical demands of presenting new work week by week.

blocks.title: Window Cleaner of the Apocalypse
blocks.description: After the end of the world, a migrant cleaner continues tending the gallery windows. Cleaning tools, samba and stubborn optimism become a way of caring for beauty amid devastation, bringing an ordinary working routine into an extraordinary future.

images.alt: Tiago Gambogi reaching towards a light among ladders
images.caption: Window Cleaner of the Apocalypse · Tiago Gambogi. Photo: Claudine Conway.

images.alt: Tiago Gambogi suspended upside down from a pole in magenta and blue light
images.caption: Window Cleaner of the Apocalypse · Tiago Gambogi. Photo: Claudine Conway.

blocks.title: Tocyn Iaith
blocks.description: A bilingual performance set in a future Wales where institutions control who can use Welsh. A valid token is required to speak it, placing the language within a bureaucratic system and raising questions about its ownership by communities.

images.caption: Tocyn Iaith · Rufus Mufasa. Photo: Hannah Jones.

images.alt: Rufus Mufasa seated on cushions with an audience close behind
images.caption: Tocyn Iaith · Rufus Mufasa. Photo: Hannah Jones.

blocks.title: Monday Morning at Machine Mart
blocks.description: Inspired by an encounter in a Cardiff gadget shop, the performance follows everyday life on the high street. Exchanges around inexpensive consumer goods become a way to examine the relationships between migration, the economy and a changing climate.

images.alt: Sahana Athreya performing Monday Morning at Machine Mart
images.caption: Monday Morning at Machine Mart · Sahana Athreya. Photo: Claudine Conway.

images.alt: Sahana Athreya standing beside a bicycle in a small shop setting
images.caption: Monday Morning at Machine Mart · Sahana Athreya. Photo: Claudine Conway.

blocks.title: The Last Place Left
blocks.description: In a near future where friendship is sold through subscriptions and attention has become a commodity, a small group enters an underground archive. It holds traces of human connection as the communities outside it begin to disappear.

images.alt: Performer gesturing across a table with a teapot and packets of biscuits, surrounded by newspapers under violet light.
images.caption: The Last Place Left · Georgia Griffiths. Photo: Jamie Panton.

images.alt: Performer seated at a typewriter among books and props while an interior is projected across the set.
images.caption: The Last Place Left · Georgia Griffiths. Photo: Jamie Panton.

blocks.title: If You Had Wings
blocks.description: Inspired by Wim Wenders’s Wings of Desire, an angel returns to a future high street devastated by war. Once a listener and comforter to its residents, she searches for human connection and the possibility of helping to build a more peaceful future.

images.alt: Performer in a pale winged costume and white sunglasses, with a red tie, under blue stage light.
images.caption: If You Had Wings · Angharad Matthews. Photo: Jamie Panton.

images.alt: Performer in a pale winged costume kneeling beside a suitcase and holding a red object against a projected backdrop.
images.caption: If You Had Wings · Angharad Matthews. Photo: Jamie Panton.

title: what the fuck is going on? (or how I see things)
summary: An authored solo performance bringing together projection, sound, satire and research into artificial intelligence and its social implications.

cover.alt: Production photograph of what the fuck is going on? (or how I see things)

meta: Commissioned by Volcano · The Shape of Things to Come · 29–31 May 2025

items: I wrote, performed, scored and designed this solo work for Volcano Theatre. Projection, music, live performance and satire formed a response to artificial intelligence and its social implications, approached from a working-class perspective.
The commission brought writing, performance, composition and visual design into one work. It was presented as part of The Shape of Things to Come in May 2025.

title: Studies for a Loving Machine
summary: An ongoing body of work exploring how energy, data, infrastructure and other systems become part of everyday experience.

cover.alt: Diagram on orange fabric: System and Behaviour connected by a waveform

items: Studies for a Loving Machine explores the systems that organise everyday life and how they are experienced through particular places. Moving image, sound, objects and live data offer different ways to encounter processes that are often difficult to see.

In September 2026, I presented work from the project and gave a talk at the 5th World Congress of Psychogeography in Swansea. The installation brought together a CRT television showing a live feed of Kilvey Hill, a composited layer of abstracted geospatial data, and sail-like forms moving in response to live weather data.

title: Jane Eyre: A Musical
summary: Associate video design and programming for the musical at Southwark Playhouse Elephant.

cover.alt: Production photograph of Jane Eyre: A Musical

meta: 28 August–24 October 2026 · Programme credit: Video Associate / Programmer

items: Charlotte Brontë’s novel becomes a musical about love, independence and the consequences of concealed truths. Jane arrives at Thornfield Hall as a governess and forms an attachment to Edward Rochester, but what she discovers there challenges the future she wants for herself. Written by John Caird and Paul Gordon, this UK premiere was co-directed by Caird and Megan McGinnis at Southwark Playhouse Elephant.

title: Ble Mae Fy Nghartref
summary: Sound, lighting and audiovisual design for Eric Ngalle Charles and Volcano’s collaboration.

cover.alt: Production photograph of Ble Mae Fy Nghartref

items: Ble Mae Fy Nghartref (Where is My Home?) brings Eric Ngalle Charles’s lived experience into a collaboration with Volcano, adapted and directed by Paul Davies. Two racist incidents become the starting point for exploring identity, belonging and the meaning of home through stories and memories. Developed with Arts Council of Wales support in April 2026, the project was shared with audiences in Swansea through two work-in-progress performances on 24 and 25 April.
